spec.description: Manhattan's 22,324 buildings raised to their surveyed roof height and coloured by era, against the MTA subway's lines and stations: how much of the city stands within walking distance of a train. Data from a public GeoLens catalogue.

options.content:
# Manhattan, by height and by subway

Two open datasets and one question: how much of Manhattan is actually within
walking distance of a train?

The buildings are NYC Open Data's footprints — 22,324 across Lower and Midtown,
each with a surveyed roof height and a year of construction. The subway is the
MTA's own open data: 29 services and 496 stations, with step-free access marked
on each. Neither was downloaded from its publisher: both came through a public
[GeoLens](https://datasets.geolibre.app) catalogue, found by following a shared
GeoLibre project, and are read here from its Parquet exports, through the
gateway's cache.

Three things worth knowing before you read the map:

- **Press play on the map's clock.** Every building carries its year, so the
  timeline runs from 1719 to today and the city rises as it plays.
- **The years belong to the lot, not to the tower.** The file's second-tallest
  building, 1,428 ft, is dated 1924 — a year when the tallest thing in New York
  was the 792 ft Woolworth Building. `construction_year` records the earliest
  structure on the site, not the one measured here.
- **The areas here are recomputed.** The file ships a `shape_area` column
  measured in Web Mercator, which at this latitude inflates every area by about
  74 %. Every square metre on this dashboard is measured from the geometry in
  UTM 18N instead.

The radius, the floor on height and the eras are dashboard variables: the
coverage figure, the table and the map all move together.

spec.rawSql:
SELECT
  bin,
  height_roof AS height_ft,
  height_roof * 0.3048 AS height_m,
  era,
  construction_year,
  -- The map's clock. Years before 1600 are the file's way of saying "no idea",
  -- and a NULL keeps those buildings out of the animation rather than parking
  -- them all on one impossible date.
  CASE WHEN construction_year >= 1600
       THEN make_timestamp(construction_year, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0) END AS time,
  round(ST_Area(ST_Transform(geometry, 'EPSG:4326', 'EPSG:32618', always_xy := true))) AS footprint_m2,
  ST_AsText(geometry) AS geom
FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/geolens/datasets/4a0bd0db-cd92-424a-8a2e-62d270ae918a.parquet')
WHERE height_roof >= CAST($minHeight AS DOUBLE)
    AND era IN (${era:singlequote})

SELECT service, service_name, ST_AsText(geometry) AS geom
FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/geolens/datasets/fd3a8635-1f38-4b51-a18f-784ea84abbbf.parquet')

SELECT
  stop_name,
  daytime_routes AS routes,
  CASE ada WHEN 1 THEN 'Full' WHEN 2 THEN 'Partial' ELSE 'None' END AS step_free,
  structure,
  ST_Y(ST_Centroid(geometry)) AS latitude,
  ST_X(ST_Centroid(geometry)) AS longitude
FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/geolens/datasets/c646ff35-82eb-442f-a524-efcbb1645023.parquet')

spec.description: Colour is the era it went up; height is the surveyed roof, in metres. Press play to watch the city arrive.
spec.title: Every building, raised to its own height

spec.rawSql:
WITH b AS (
  SELECT bin, height_roof,
         ST_Transform(ST_Centroid(geometry), 'EPSG:4326', 'EPSG:32618', always_xy := true) AS pt,
         ST_Area(ST_Transform(geometry, 'EPSG:4326', 'EPSG:32618', always_xy := true)) AS footprint_m2
  FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/geolens/datasets/4a0bd0db-cd92-424a-8a2e-62d270ae918a.parquet')
  WHERE height_roof >= CAST($minHeight AS DOUBLE)
    AND era IN (${era:singlequote})
), s AS (
  SELECT stop_name, daytime_routes, borough, ada,
         ST_Transform(geometry, 'EPSG:4326', 'EPSG:32618', always_xy := true) AS pt
  FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/geolens/datasets/c646ff35-82eb-442f-a524-efcbb1645023.parquet')
)
, tagged AS (
  SELECT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM s WHERE ST_DWithin(b.pt, s.pt, CAST($radius AS DOUBLE))
  ) AS served
  FROM b
)
SELECT
  round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE served) / nullif(count(*), 0), 1) AS "Within reach",
  count(*) FILTER (WHERE served) AS "Buildings served",
  count(*) AS "Buildings shown"
FROM tagged

WITH b AS (
  SELECT bin, height_roof,
         ST_Transform(ST_Centroid(geometry), 'EPSG:4326', 'EPSG:32618', always_xy := true) AS pt,
         ST_Area(ST_Transform(geometry, 'EPSG:4326', 'EPSG:32618', always_xy := true)) AS footprint_m2
  FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/geolens/datasets/4a0bd0db-cd92-424a-8a2e-62d270ae918a.parquet')
  WHERE height_roof >= CAST($minHeight AS DOUBLE)
    AND era IN (${era:singlequote})
), s AS (
  SELECT stop_name, daytime_routes, borough, ada,
         ST_Transform(geometry, 'EPSG:4326', 'EPSG:32618', always_xy := true) AS pt
  FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/geolens/datasets/c646ff35-82eb-442f-a524-efcbb1645023.parquet')
)
SELECT
  s.stop_name AS "Station",
  s.daytime_routes AS "Routes",
  CASE s.borough WHEN 'M' THEN 'Manhattan' WHEN 'Bk' THEN 'Brooklyn'
                 WHEN 'Bx' THEN 'Bronx'    WHEN 'Q'  THEN 'Queens'
                 WHEN 'SI' THEN 'Staten Island' END AS "Borough",
  CASE s.ada WHEN 1 THEN 'Full' WHEN 2 THEN 'Partial' ELSE 'None' END AS "Step-free",
  count(b.bin) AS "Buildings",
  round(max(b.height_roof)) AS "Tallest (ft)",
  round(sum(b.footprint_m2)) AS "Footprint (m2)"
FROM s LEFT JOIN b ON ST_DWithin(s.pt, b.pt, CAST($radius AS DOUBLE))
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4
HAVING count(b.bin) > 0
ORDER BY 5 DESC

spec.description: Buildings whose centre falls within $radius m of the station, and what they add up to.
spec.title: Stations, by how much of the city they stand in

spec.rawSql:
-- Every era, whatever the "Built in" filter says: the chart is where eras are
-- picked, so the ones left out stay on it, in grey, to be clicked back.
SELECT
  era,
  count(*) AS buildings,
  round(avg(height_roof), 1) AS avg_height_ft
FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/geolens/datasets/4a0bd0db-cd92-424a-8a2e-62d270ae918a.parquet')
WHERE height_roof >= CAST($minHeight AS DOUBLE)
GROUP BY era
ORDER BY min(coalesce(construction_year, 9999))
